## See your first result

**mcp-geo** is a free, self-hostable MCP server for measuring brand mentions and, where providers return them, source citations across supported AI answer surfaces. It helps SEO practitioners and agencies compare observations by engine and inspect the underlying evidence. A scan is a point-in-time sample, not a guaranteed ranking or citation outcome.

[![Example AI visibility report](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AKzar1el/mcp-geo/main/docs/demo-report-hero.png)](https://github.com/AKzar1el/mcp-geo/blob/main/docs/demo-report-full.png)

*[Open the full example report](https://github.com/AKzar1el/mcp-geo/blob/main/docs/demo-report-full.png) · [How the methodology works](https://github.com/AKzar1el/mcp-geo/blob/main/docs/ai-visibility-audit-methodology.md)*. This is an example report generated through the MCP tools, not a customer testimonial or a promised result.

**Your first local scan, after connecting the stdio MCP server:**

1. **Track:** ask your MCP client to run `track_brand` with your own `brand_id`, name, domain, and ideally a precise `category`. By default it creates three provider-free category-anchored starter questions, not a validated measurement sample. Without a category, its brand-name placeholders can bias scores: replace those prompts before scanning. The read-only `list_prompts.prompt_review` advisory flags missing categories and prompts naming the tracked brand; it does not certify that other questions are representative.
2. **Measure:** after reviewing and, when needed, replacing the starter questions with representative independent buyer prompts, run `refresh_brand` with that `brand_id`. **Live scans use your provider API keys and may incur charges.** Engines without keys are skipped; Google AI Mode requires a separate explicit opt-in. Retrying after a partial scan makes fresh provider requests for **all active prompts** on the selected engines, including ones that previously succeeded; old successful answers are not reused as new evidence. Review partial coverage with `check_visibility` before choosing whether and when to retry.
3. **Inspect:** run `check_visibility` with the same `brand_id` to view available per-engine scores and evidence. Use `get_citations` to inspect citation records where providers supply sources.

Winning prompts now distinguish `engines_mentioned_in` (brand named in the answer) from `engines_with_brand_link` (the answer or provider sources included a brand-domain link). The older `engines_cited_in` field is retained for compatibility but counts **mentions**, not verified citations. A linked source alone is not scored as an answer mention.

`check_visibility.prompt_set_comparability` warns when the latest scored observations include prompts no longer in the active prompt set, such as after replacing buyer-intent questions. Its `engines_with_retired_prompt_evidence` identifies affected engines without rewriting historical measurements. Missing or failed answers are handled separately by per-engine `coverage`, not misclassified as retired prompts. Rerun the affected engines when a current-prompt comparison is needed; this uses your configured providers and may incur charges.

`check_visibility.configuration_comparability` separately identifies engines whose latest scans started before the tracked brand's most recent settings update. Historical scores are not silently recomputed under a new domain, name, alias, exclusion, or competitor list. This is a conservative warning: the database does not retain which settings changed, so a refresh-cadence-only edit can also trigger it. Review the change before interpreting old scores as current-brand evidence; rescanning uses your provider keys and may incur charges.

**Choose your setup:** [Quick Install and client-specific instructions](#quick-install) for local MCP hosts · [Getting Started](#getting-started) for provider keys and optional Cloudflare hosting · [What the report contains](#what-it-produces) · [Privacy](#privacy-policy). Hosted remote MCP deployments manage brands through their protected admin routes rather than local `track_brand`.


## Quick Install

Runs locally over stdio with your own API keys. Brands, scan history, and cached responses are stored on your machine; scan prompts are sent to the AI providers you configure (see [Privacy Policy](#privacy-policy)). Set at least one engine key (`OPENAI_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `PERPLEXITY_API_KEY`, `XAI_API_KEY`, `SERPAPI_API_KEY`); engines without a key skip gracefully.

**Runtime:** Node.js 22.13+ (CI exercises Node 22 and 24).

**Portable Agent Skill (optional):** Assistants supporting [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io/) can install this repository's GEO workflow guidance using `npx skills add AKzar1el/mcp-geo --skill mcp-geo`. This installs instructions only, not the MCP server or provider credentials; configure `npx -y @digestseo/mcp-geo` separately in your MCP host.

**Claude Desktop / any MCP client (npx):**

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "digestseo": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@digestseo/mcp-geo"],
      "env": {
        "OPENAI_API_KEY": "sk-...",
        "GEMINI_API_KEY": "your_key_here"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

**ChatGPT (remote MCP):** ChatGPT does not connect directly to local STDIO MCP servers. For ChatGPT, use the [self-hosted remote MCP setup](#chatgpt-remote-mcp) below, or the [OpenAI Secure MCP Tunnel setup](#chatgpt-localprivate-via-openai-secure-mcp-tunnel) for a server running on a local/private machine. The public `geo-mcp.digestseo.com/mcp` endpoint is not a turnkey no-key fresh-scan service.

**Perplexity Computer (remote MCP):** Perplexity Computer supports custom remote MCP connectors on eligible plans. After self-hosting mcp-geo, open **Account settings > Connectors > + Custom connector**, choose **Remote**, name it `digestseo`, and enter your own deployment's `https://<worker-host>/mcp` URL. Use the connector's OAuth option for the Worker flow; configure the required `CONNECT_SECRET` in your Worker and enter it in the browser gate during connection. Do not use the public `geo-mcp.digestseo.com/mcp` endpoint as a turnkey no-key scan service. See Perplexity's current [Computer connector guidance](https://www.perplexity.ai/changelog/what-we-shipped---march-13-2026).

**Perplexity Portable Computer (local STDIO):** On supported hardware with a Perplexity Pro/Max local model, open **Settings > MCP servers > Add server > Local (stdio)** and name the server `digestseo`. Portable requires an **absolute Command path**: on Windows use `C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe` with arguments `/d`, `/s`, `/c`, and `npx -y @digestseo/mcp-geo` (each on its own line); on Linux use the absolute `npx` path with `-y` and `@digestseo/mcp-geo` as separate arguments. Select **Test**, then **Add**. Node.js 22.13+ is required. No provider keys are needed for tool discovery; engine-backed scans can incur provider charges. Portable's local tools are distinct from cloud Computer's Remote/OAuth connector. See the [local Portable setup guide](llms-install.md#perplexity-portable-computer-local-stdio) and [Perplexity's official instructions](https://www.perplexity.ai/help-center/en/articles/20260915-what-is-portable-computer).

**Replit Agent (remote MCP):** after self-hosting mcp-geo, open **Integrations -> MCP Servers for Replit Agent -> Add MCP server**, name it `digestseo`, and enter your own deployment's `https://<worker-host>/mcp` URL. Choose the OAuth flow when prompted: Replit supports OAuth dynamic client registration (DCR), which the self-hosted Worker exposes through its standard discovery and registration endpoints. Select **Test & Save**, then complete the browser authorization step with the required `CONNECT_SECRET`. Replit supports remote HTTPS MCP servers rather than this package's local stdio process, so use your configured Worker URL and do not treat the public `geo-mcp.digestseo.com/mcp` endpoint as a turnkey provider-key service. See Replit's current [MCP guide](https://docs.replit.com/features/mcp/overview).

```bash
claude mcp add --transport stdio digestseo -s user --env GEMINI_API_KEY=your_key_here -- npx -y @digestseo/mcp-geo
```

/plugin install digestseo-geo@digestseo-mcp
```

**Reading combined scores:** `check_visibility` reports each engine's observation time and a `freshness` range for the combined score. `mixed_age_warning=true` means at least one engine was measured 24 hours or more before the newest engine; `older_engines` identifies which. The overall score still averages available engine scores, not a synchronized new scan. Use `refresh_brand` to update old measurements before comparisons; this may incur configured provider API costs.

**Search evidence vs. model-only answers:** `check_visibility.measurement_scope` separates the mean visibility score from engines whose live request uses search/SERP (`search_requested`) from engines without live search (`model_only`). The Claude and Gemini adapters currently use model-only generation; ChatGPT batch runs are also model-only. Each `per_engine` record carries its `measurement_mode`. `mixed_modes=true` means the legacy `overall_score` blends these unlike observations. Use optional `check_visibility` `run_mode='live'` or `run_mode='batch'` to compare stored scans of one dispatch mode; omission preserves the latest usable run per engine across modes. An engine with no usable scans in the requested mode is excluded rather than borrowing evidence from the other mode. `live` does not imply search evidence (Claude and Gemini remain model-only). Even `search_requested` does **not** prove that a response returned verifiable citations: inspect the actual evidence through `get_citations`, and never present model-generated links as independently observed AI-search citations. No additional provider calls are made to calculate this disclosure.

## See your first result

**mcp-geo** is a free, self-hostable MCP server for measuring brand mentions and, where providers return them, source citations across supported AI answer surfaces. It helps SEO practitioners and agencies compare observations by engine and inspect the underlying evidence. A scan is a point-in-time sample, not a guaranteed ranking or citation outcome.

[![Example AI visibility report](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AKzar1el/mcp-geo/main/docs/demo-report-hero.png)](https://github.com/AKzar1el/mcp-geo/blob/main/docs/demo-report-full.png)

*[Open the full example report](https://github.com/AKzar1el/mcp-geo/blob/main/docs/demo-report-full.png) · [How the methodology works](https://github.com/AKzar1el/mcp-geo/blob/main/docs/ai-visibility-audit-methodology.md)*. This is an example report generated through the MCP tools, not a customer testimonial or a promised result.

**Your first local scan, after connecting the stdio MCP server:**

1. **Track:** ask your MCP client to run `track_brand` with your own `brand_id`, name, domain, and ideally a precise `category`. By default it creates three provider-free category-anchored starter questions, not a validated measurement sample. Without a category, its brand-name placeholders can bias scores: replace those prompts before scanning. The read-only `list_prompts.prompt_review` advisory flags missing categories and prompts naming the tracked brand; it does not certify that other questions are representative.
2. **Measure:** after reviewing and, when needed, replacing the starter questions with representative independent buyer prompts, run `refresh_brand` with that `brand_id`. **Live scans use your provider API keys and may incur charges.** Engines without keys are skipped; Google AI Mode requires a separate explicit opt-in. Retrying after a partial scan makes fresh provider requests for **all active prompts** on the selected engines, including ones that previously succeeded; old successful answers are not reused as new evidence. Review partial coverage with `check_visibility` before choosing whether and when to retry.
3. **Inspect:** run `check_visibility` with the same `brand_id` to view available per-engine scores and evidence. Use `get_citations` to inspect citation records where providers supply sources.

Winning prompts now distinguish `engines_mentioned_in` (brand named in the answer) from `engines_with_brand_link` (the answer or provider sources included a brand-domain link). The older `engines_cited_in` field is retained for compatibility but counts **mentions**, not verified citations. A linked source alone is not scored as an answer mention.

`check_visibility.prompt_set_comparability` warns when the latest scored observations include prompts no longer in the active prompt set, such as after replacing buyer-intent questions. Its `engines_with_retired_prompt_evidence` identifies affected engines without rewriting historical measurements. Missing or failed answers are handled separately by per-engine `coverage`, not misclassified as retired prompts. Rerun the affected engines when a current-prompt comparison is needed; this uses your configured providers and may incur charges.

`check_visibility.configuration_comparability` separately identifies engines whose latest scans started before the tracked brand's most recent settings update. Historical scores are not silently recomputed under a new domain, name, alias, exclusion, or competitor list. This is a conservative warning: the database does not retain which settings changed, so a refresh-cadence-only edit can also trigger it. Review the change before interpreting old scores as current-brand evidence; rescanning uses your provider keys and may incur charges.

**Choose your setup:** [Quick Install and client-specific instructions](#quick-install) for local MCP hosts · [Getting Started](#getting-started) for provider keys and optional Cloudflare hosting · [What the report contains](#what-it-produces) · [Privacy](#privacy-policy). Hosted remote MCP deployments manage brands through their protected admin routes rather than local `track_brand`.
